# Reference Skill (control-pulse handshake -- back-to-back DV case)

# Skill: Control-pulse handshake — one-shot commands and back-to-back operations

Command and status handshakes across a control boundary are a recurring source
of silent bugs: a START pulse that re-triggers with stale config, a DONE level
that a fast consumer samples from the PREVIOUS operation. This skill is the
contract for one-shot command pulses and level status across back-to-back
operations. Apply it whenever a block is armed by a START/GO and reports a
DONE/status (a register-mapped accelerator, an FSM launched by a control pulse,
any block that runs discrete operations back to back).

## One-shot command pulses (START / GO / KICK)

A one-shot command must be **cleared by the consumer's OBSERVED ACCEPTANCE**,
never held until the block is idle again:

- The producer asserts START for one cycle (or holds it) and the consumer
  latches the request and its accompanying config on the accepting edge.
- Clear/deassert START when the consumer's **acceptance is observed** — e.g. the
  block asserts `busy`/`ack` and the producer sees it — NOT on "block idle".
- **Never** hold START asserted until the block returns to idle: when the block
  finishes and drops `busy`, a still-asserted START **immediately re-triggers**
  the operation, now with whatever (stale) config is on the bus. That spurious
  re-launch is the classic auto-re-trigger bug.
- Latch the config **with** the accepted START. Do not let the datapath read
  live config registers mid-operation; a back-to-back writer may have already
  changed them for the NEXT operation.

## DONE / status levels across back-to-back boundaries

A DONE/valid/status **level** exposed across operations must be qualified so a
consumer cannot read the PREVIOUS operation's result as this one's:

- Gate any exposed DONE/status on **"busy seen since THIS operation's START"** —
  the block must have entered busy for the current launch before its DONE is
  visible. A bare `done` level that was left high from the prior operation is
  read as an early (wrong-operation) completion by a fast poller.
- Clear DONE at the accepted START of the next operation (before asserting busy),
  so there is no window where the old DONE and the new START coexist.

## Decomposition tax — do NOT pay cycles at registered boundaries

Decomposing a design into modules and control states is correct, but each
throwaway registered boundary adds a cycle to EVERY op and shows up directly in
the delivery-time measured cyc/op (see the throughput_budget_contract skill and
the measured-throughput gate). Three specific wastes, each proven to cost real
cycles against a golden that avoids them:

1. **Accept the command on the FINAL cycle of the incoming write, not a
   registered cycle after it.** When a START/command is delivered as the last
   beat/shift of a bus write, decode and latch it MID-SHIFT — on the same edge
   that completes the write — so the datapath launches the next cycle. A design
   that first registers "write done", THEN in a following state decodes the
   command, pays one full cycle per op for nothing.
2. **No single-purpose bridge / wait state between two registered
   inter-module handshakes.** If module A registers its output and module B
   registers its input, a state that exists only to "hand the token across" is
   a dead cycle — FOLD the accept into the consuming state (B samples A's
   registered valid directly and advances). A `WAIT_FOR_B` / `BRIDGE` state
   whose only body is `state <= NEXT` is the tell. (This class cost +2.)
3. **Drive status/DONE output PINS combinationally from the status register —
   never re-register them in a pin adapter.** A top-level/port adapter that
   samples the internal `done`/`status` reg into ANOTHER flop before driving the
   pin delays every completion by a cycle for the poller, inflating the measured
   op window. The pin is `assign done_pin = status_q[DONE_BIT];`, not a second
   registered copy. (A prior design paid +5 re-registering status through the
   adapter.)

These are not micro-optimizations to defer — they are the difference between the
declared cyc/op and a delivered design that misses it by a handful of cycles per
op. Record the accept/commit timing in the uArch spec (Section 3.3) so it is a
testable contract, not an accident of decomposition.

## Per-block DV MUST include a back-to-back case

The block's testbench MUST cover a back-to-back scenario, because the single-op
test passes even when both bugs above are present:

- Issue a new START within a few cycles of the prior DONE, with a **DIFFERENT
  config** than the first operation.
- Assert the second operation uses the **new config** (not the latched/stale
  first config) — check an output that depends on the changed config value.
- Assert DONE for the second operation is **not visible early** — the consumer
  must not observe a completion before the block has taken busy for the second
  START (i.e. the first operation's DONE must not leak into the second).
- Include the degenerate timing: START asserted the same cycle DONE deasserts.

Record in the uArch spec (Section 3.3, Control Logic) exactly when START is
accepted, when it is cleared (the observed-acceptance condition), and when DONE
becomes valid and is cleared — as an explicit, testable timing contract.

GOLDEN MODEL IMPORTS:
A wrapper module named ``<block_name>_model`` is available on PYTHONPATH.

ORACLE FIDELITY -- THE BLOCK MODEL IS THE SOLE ORACLE (MANDATORY):
The imported ``<block_name>_model`` is the authoritative reference. Your

  - Compute every expected output from the model object (call it on the test

``coeff_levels_word``, ``rtl_selected_payload``, a hand-coded DCT/quant/entropy coding,

match and DV passes GREEN while the design is byte-wrong at integration. This

AXI-STREAM HANDSHAKING -- CRITICAL:
When the DUT has AXI-Stream input (s_tvalid/s_tready) and output
(m_tvalid/m_tready), you MUST avoid deadlocks:

  - ALWAYS drive ``m_tready = 1`` BEFORE sending data on the input interface.
    Many RTL designs gate s_tready on m_tready (e.g.
    ``assign s_tready = !m_tvalid || m_tready``).  If m_tready is 0 when
    the output buffer fills, s_tready drops to 0 and the testbench hangs

    grader (post-edge): drive inputs and out_ready for the cycle, `await
    RisingEdge`, `await ReadOnly`, count a word accepted only if `in_ready`
    reads 1 after the edge (re-offer it otherwise), count an output beat
    consumed only if `out_valid` reads 1 after the edge with the `out_ready`

    output backpressure over several seeds. Port names alone do not establish
    this exception. Otherwise use the standard edge-handshake rules below
    for AXI-Stream, srdy/drdy, and other synchronous valid/ready channels.

    ``tvalid/tdata/tlast`` before the rising edge that may accept the beat,
    sample settled ``tready`` before that same rising edge, then deassert

        async def send_axis(dut, data, last=0, max_wait=1000):
            await FallingEdge(dut.clk)
            dut.s_axis_tdata.value = int(data)
            dut.s_axis_tlast.value = int(last)
            dut.s_axis_tvalid.value = 1
            for _ in range(max_wait):
                await ReadOnly()  # settle combinational ready after our drives
                ready = int(dut.s_axis_tready.value)
                await RisingEdge(dut.clk)
                if ready:
                    await FallingEdge(dut.clk)  # change drives away from accept edge
                    dut.s_axis_tvalid.value = 0
                    dut.s_axis_tdata.value = 0
                    dut.s_axis_tlast.value = 0

# Reference Skill (control-pulse handshake -- back-to-back DV case)

# Skill: Control-pulse handshake — one-shot commands and back-to-back operations

Command and status handshakes across a control boundary are a recurring source
of silent bugs: a START pulse that re-triggers with stale config, a DONE level
that a fast consumer samples from the PREVIOUS operation. This skill is the
contract for one-shot command pulses and level status across back-to-back
operations. Apply it whenever a block is armed by a START/GO and reports a
DONE/status (a register-mapped accelerator, an FSM launched by a control pulse,
any block that runs discrete operations back to back).

## One-shot command pulses (START / GO / KICK)

A one-shot command must be **cleared by the consumer's OBSERVED ACCEPTANCE**,
never held until the block is idle again:

- The producer asserts START for one cycle (or holds it) and the consumer
  latches the request and its accompanying config on the accepting edge.
- Clear/deassert START when the consumer's **acceptance is observed** — e.g. the
  block asserts `busy`/`ack` and the producer sees it — NOT on "block idle".
- **Never** hold START asserted until the block returns to idle: when the block
  finishes and drops `busy`, a still-asserted START **immediately re-triggers**
  the operation, now with whatever (stale) config is on the bus. That spurious
  re-launch is the classic auto-re-trigger bug.
- Latch the config **with** the accepted START. Do not let the datapath read
  live config registers mid-operation; a back-to-back writer may have already
  changed them for the NEXT operation.

## DONE / status levels across back-to-back boundaries

A DONE/valid/status **level** exposed across operations must be qualified so a
consumer cannot read the PREVIOUS operation's result as this one's:

- Gate any exposed DONE/status on **"busy seen since THIS operation's START"** —
  the block must have entered busy for the current launch before its DONE is
  visible. A bare `done` level that was left high from the prior operation is
  read as an early (wrong-operation) completion by a fast poller.
- Clear DONE at the accepted START of the next operation (before asserting busy),
  so there is no window where the old DONE and the new START coexist.

## Decomposition tax — do NOT pay cycles at registered boundaries

Decomposing a design into modules and control states is correct, but each
throwaway registered boundary adds a cycle to EVERY op and shows up directly in
the delivery-time measured cyc/op (see the throughput_budget_contract skill and
the measured-throughput gate). Three specific wastes, each proven to cost real
cycles against a golden that avoids them:

1. **Accept the command on the FINAL cycle of the incoming write, not a
   registered cycle after it.** When a START/command is delivered as the last
   beat/shift of a bus write, decode and latch it MID-SHIFT — on the same edge
   that completes the write — so the datapath launches the next cycle. A design
   that first registers "write done", THEN in a following state decodes the
   command, pays one full cycle per op for nothing.
2. **No single-purpose bridge / wait state between two registered
   inter-module handshakes.** If module A registers its output and module B
   registers its input, a state that exists only to "hand the token across" is
   a dead cycle — FOLD the accept into the consuming state (B samples A's
   registered valid directly and advances). A `WAIT_FOR_B` / `BRIDGE` state
   whose only body is `state <= NEXT` is the tell. (This class cost +2.)
3. **Drive status/DONE output PINS combinationally from the status register —
   never re-register them in a pin adapter.** A top-level/port adapter that
   samples the internal `done`/`status` reg into ANOTHER flop before driving the
   pin delays every completion by a cycle for the poller, inflating the measured
   op window. The pin is `assign done_pin = status_q[DONE_BIT];`, not a second
   registered copy. (A prior design paid +5 re-registering status through the
   adapter.)

These are not micro-optimizations to defer — they are the difference between the
declared cyc/op and a delivered design that misses it by a handful of cycles per
op. Record the accept/commit timing in the uArch spec (Section 3.3) so it is a
testable contract, not an accident of decomposition.

## Per-block DV MUST include a back-to-back case

The block's testbench MUST cover a back-to-back scenario, because the single-op
test passes even when both bugs above are present:

- Issue a new START within a few cycles of the prior DONE, with a **DIFFERENT
  config** than the first operation.
- Assert the second operation uses the **new config** (not the latched/stale
  first config) — check an output that depends on the changed config value.
- Assert DONE for the second operation is **not visible early** — the consumer
  must not observe a completion before the block has taken busy for the second
  START (i.e. the first operation's DONE must not leak into the second).
- Include the degenerate timing: START asserted the same cycle DONE deasserts.

Record in the uArch spec (Section 3.3, Control Logic) exactly when START is
accepted, when it is cleared (the observed-acceptance condition), and when DONE
becomes valid and is cleared — as an explicit, testable timing contract.

# `alu32` Microarchitecture Specification

## 1. Block Overview

- **Block name:** `alu32`
- **Function:** `alu32` is a stateless 32-bit combinational arithmetic/logic unit. It accepts two 32-bit operands and a 3-bit operation selector, and produces one 32-bit result. The supported operations are modulo-`2^32` addition, modulo-`2^32` subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, and bitwise XOR. No carry, borrow, signed-overflow, zero, or comparison flags are generated because none were requested.
- **Latency:** 0 clock cycles. The output changes combinationally after an input change and settles after the combinational propagation delay.
- **Throughput:** One independent operation per integration clock cycle (`1.0 operation/cycle`) when placed between synchronous source and destination registers. There is no internal initiation restriction.
- **Pipeline depth:** 0 registered stages; one logical combinational evaluation stage.
- **Interface protocol:** Simple dedicated pins. The supplied requirements describe a standalone ALU and do not require a bus, streaming protocol, valid/ready flow control, or packet framing. No separate ERS, frozen interface-contract file, FRD, block diagram, or neighboring-block description exists in the workspace; consequently, Section 2 establishes the minimal standalone port contract needed by the requested function.
- **Golden model:** No Python golden model exists. The Boolean and modulo-arithmetic equations in Section 4 are the functional reference for RTL and DV.
- **Clock/reset:** The block contains no state, registers, latches, memories, or FSM. Therefore `clk` and `rst_n` are intentionally absent. The requirement for synchronous active-low `rst_n` applies only when state is present.

## 2. Interface Specification

All ports are unhandshaked dedicated pins. Inputs form one atomic combinational tuple: `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `operation` must refer to the same requested operation. `result` is meaningful whenever those three inputs are stable; there is no separate validity signal.

| Port | Direction | Width | Protocol | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `operand_a` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | First operand, `operand_a[31:0]`. Treated as an unscaled 32-bit bit vector. For ADD/SUB it participates in modulo-`2^32` arithmetic; the same bits may also be interpreted as two's-complement by a consumer because the low 32 result bits are identical. |
| `operand_b` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | Second operand, `operand_b[31:0]`, with the same numeric interpretation as `operand_a`. |
| `operation` | Input | 3 | Dedicated pins | Operation code: `3'b000` ADD, `3'b001` SUB, `3'b010` AND, `3'b011` OR, `3'b100` XOR, and `3'b101` through `3'b111` RESERVED. |
| `result` | Output | 32 | Dedicated pins | Combinational result. ADD and SUB return the low 32 bits (wrap modulo `2^32`); AND/OR/XOR operate independently on each bit. Reserved operation codes return `32'h0000_0000`. |

There are no implicit ports, flags, clock, reset, valid/ready, or error sidebands. If a later integration contract requires differently named ports or flags, the contract and this specification must be revised together; aliases must not be added silently.

## 3. Microarchitecture

### 3.1 Top-Level Block Diagram

```text
                         operation[2:0]
                              |
                              v
                       +--------------+
                       | exact opcode |
                       | decoder      |
                       +------+-------+
                              |
             sub_sel ---------+------------------------------+
                |                                            |
                v                                            v
operand_b --> [32 XOR gates] --> b_mod[31:0]         +----------------+
                ^                                    | AND / OR / XOR |
                |                                    | 32-bit logic   |
                +-- {32{sub_sel}}                    +-------+--------+
                                                            |
operand_a --> zero extend --+                                |
                            v                                |
                       +-----------+                         |
b_mod --> zero extend ->| 33-bit   |--> arith_ext[32:0]      |
sub_sel --> carry-in -->| adder     |--> arith_low[31:0]      |
                       +-----+-----+                         |
                             |                               |
                             +---------------+---------------+
                                             v
                                      +-------------+
operation[2:0] ---------------------->| 32-bit      |--> result[31:0]
                                      | result mux  |
                                      +-------------+
```

The add and subtract operations share one 33-bit adder. The bitwise functions may be synthesized as parallel gates feeding the result mux. The opcode decode uses exact equality comparisons; no wildcard (`casex`/`casez`) decode is permitted.

### 3.2 Datapath

#### Number formats

- `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `result` are plain 32-bit unscaled bit vectors; fixed-point Q notation is not applicable.
- Arithmetic is modulo `2^32`. This definition is valid for both unsigned and two's-complement operand interpretations when only the low 32 result bits are retained.
- Intermediate widening uses zero extension because the implementation is explicitly performing unsigned modulo arithmetic. There is no implicit signed cast.

#### Shared add/sub datapath

Define these exact combinational nodes:

```text
sub_sel       = (operation == 3'b001)                 // 1 bit
a_ext         = {1'b0, operand_a}                     // 33 bits unsigned
b_mod         = operand_b XOR {32{sub_sel}}           // 32 bits
b_mod_ext     = {1'b0, b_mod}                         // 33 bits unsigned
carry_in_ext  = {32'b0, sub_sel}                      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_ext     = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_low     = arith_ext[31:0]                       // 32 bits
```

- For ADD, `sub_sel=0`, so `arith_ext = {0,A}+{0,B}`.
- For SUB, `sub_sel=1`, so the low 32 bits implement `A + ~B + 1 = A-B (mod 2^32)`.
- `arith_ext[32]` is deliberately discarded. For ADD it is the carry-out. For SUB no borrow/carry flag is exposed.
- No saturation or rounding occurs. Width reduction from 33 to 32 bits is explicit truncation of the most-significant carry bit, producing wraparound modulo `2^32`.

#### Bit-width derivation

| Node/operation | Input range | Mathematical range | Hardware width and policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a_ext`, `b_mod_ext` | `0` to `2^32-1` | Same | 33-bit unsigned, zero-extended |
| ADD exact sum | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `0..2^33-2` | 33-bit unsigned `arith_ext`; output truncates to 32 bits (wrap) |
| SUB mathematical difference | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `-(2^32-1)..+(2^32-1)` | Implemented by a 33-bit unsigned two's-complement adder; low 32 bits are exact modulo-`2^32` difference |
| AND/OR/XOR | Two 32-bit vectors | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits, no growth, no overflow |
| Opcode result mux | Five 32-bit candidates plus zero | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits; no truncation |

#### Bitwise datapath and result selection

```text
and_result = operand_a & operand_b     // 32 bits
or_result  = operand_a | operand_b     // 32 bits
xor_result = operand_a ^ operand_b     // 32 bits
```

The final combinational selection is:

| `operation` | Mnemonic | `result` equation |
|---:|---|---|
| `3'b000` | ADD | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=0` |
| `3'b001` | SUB | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=1` |
| `3'b010` | AND | `operand_a & operand_b` |
| `3'b011` | OR | `operand_a | operand_b` |
| `3'b100` | XOR | `operand_a ^ operand_b` |
| `3'b101` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b110` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b111` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |

RTL must assign a default of `32'h0000_0000` before or in the `default` arm of a complete combinational `case` so no latch is inferred.

### 3.3 Control Logic

No FSM is required. There is no sequential control, command pulse, busy/done status, handshake, buffering, or backpressure.

The only control is combinational opcode decode:

- `sub_sel` is asserted only for `operation == 3'b001`.
- A complete `case (operation)` selects exactly one result equation.
- Reserved binary opcode values select zero.
- `operation` is consumed in the same combinational interval in which it is decoded, so there is no later FSM state and no decoded decision that needs to be latched.
- Implement using `always @*` with blocking assignments, or equivalent continuous assignments compatible with Verilog-2005. Do not use SystemVerilog `always_comb`, `logic`, `unique case`, or enumerated types.

### 3.4 Storage Elements

There are no registers, arrays, FIFOs, register files, ROMs, LUT memories, SRAMs, or other storage elements. Boolean gates used for bitwise operations are logic, not a lookup-table memory. Accordingly, the memory manifest is empty.

- **Registers:** none.
- **Memories:** none.
- **FSM state:** none.
- **`flip_flop_budget`:** exactly `0 FF`. The implemented RTL must remain combinational and synthesis must report zero inferred latches and zero inferred flip-flops for this module.
- **`sram_budget`:** `0 bits (0 KiB)`, zero macros.
- **ROM budget:** `0 bits`.

No storage geometry reaches the 2-Kbit SRAM threshold, and no CoreSmith memory primitive is needed.

## 4. Algorithm Mapping

No Python golden model was supplied and none exists. The following mapping is from the requested functional description to hardware; it is the complete reference behavior.

| Functional requirement | Hardware mapping |
|---|---|
| 32-bit addition | One shared 33-bit adder, `A+B`, followed by explicit selection of bits `[31:0]` |
| 32-bit subtraction | The same 33-bit adder using `A+(~B)+1`; select bits `[31:0]` |
| Bitwise AND | 32 parallel two-input AND functions |
| Bitwise OR | 32 parallel two-input OR functions |
| Bitwise XOR | 32 parallel two-input XOR functions |
| Choose operation | Complete 3-bit combinational opcode decoder and 32-bit result mux |
| Unsupported opcode | Constant-zero mux input |

There are no loops, dynamic lists, exceptions, dictionaries, floating-point values, divisions, shifts, casts, coefficient tables, or iteration-order semantics to map.

Reference equations for bit-exact verification, with all operations masked to 32 bits:

```text
ADD: result = (operand_a + operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
SUB: result = (operand_a - operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
AND: result =  operand_a & operand_b
OR:  result =  operand_a | operand_b
XOR: result =  operand_a ^ operand_b
RESERVED: result = 32'h0000_0000
```

### 4a. Cross-Block Semantic Invariants (MANDATORY)

No architecture connection graph or neighboring block is supplied. Therefore there is no named cross-block feedback, context, packet ordering, frame geometry, or adaptive state to preserve. It is safe for this block to be stateless because every output is a pure function of the current input tuple and no prior operation affects a later one. The interface-level invariants below are nevertheless mandatory for any eventual producer and consumer.

- **Applies to ports/state:** `operand_a`, `operand_b`, `operation`, and `result`; no internal state.
- **Invariant:** `result` must be computed from the same concurrently presented values of all three inputs. Mixing an old operand with a new opcode is outside the interface contract.
- **Golden reference point:** The equations in Section 4; no Python golden model exists.

- **Update/consume timing:** Combinational. A consumer may sample `result` only after all inputs and the combinational path meet its setup requirement at the consumer's capture edge.

- There are no registers or memories to initialize.
- There is no reset port. The specified synchronous active-low reset convention is inapplicable because the block is entirely combinational.
- There is no multi-cycle initialization sequence.
- During a chip-level reset, `result` continues to be the combinational function of the ALU inputs. The integrating source must drive known inputs if a known reset-time result is required.

from cocotb.triggers import Timer

# WARNING: model wrapper unavailable; TB-local reference may drift from the block model
# The alu32 uArch explicitly states that no Python golden model exists and
# defines its equations as the authoritative functional reference.
try:
    from alu32_model import alu32 as _golden_alu32
except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
    if exc.name != "alu32_model":
        raise
    _golden_alu32 = None


_DV_SEED = int(os.environ.get("CORESMITH_DV_SEED", "0"), 0)
_MASK32 = (1 << 32) - 1
_SETTLE_NS = 1


def _spec_reference(operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int) -> int:
    """Fallback oracle: the exact equations designated by uArch section 4."""
    operand_a &= _MASK32
    operand_b &= _MASK32
    operation &= 0x7
    if operation == 0:
        return (operand_a + operand_b) & _MASK32
    if operation == 1:
        return (operand_a - operand_b) & _MASK32
    if operation == 2:
        return operand_a & operand_b
    if operation == 3:
        return operand_a | operand_b
    if operation == 4:
        return operand_a ^ operand_b
    return 0


def _model_result(operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int) -> int:
    """Call the supplied model when present, otherwise use its specified fallback."""
    if _golden_alu32 is not None:
        return int(_golden_alu32(int(operand_a), int(operand_b), int(operation))) & _MASK32
    return _spec_reference(operand_a, operand_b, operation)


async def _drive_and_check(dut, operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int,
                           *, context: str) -> int:
    operand_a = int(operand_a) & _MASK32
    operand_b = int(operand_b) & _MASK32
    operation = int(operation) & 0x7
    expected = _model_result(operand_a, operand_b, operation)

    dut.operand_a.value = operand_a
    dut.operand_b.value = operand_b
    dut.operation.value = operation
    await Timer(_SETTLE_NS, unit="ns")

    actual = int(dut.result.value)
    assert actual == expected, (
        f"{context}: A=0x{operand_a:08x}, B=0x{operand_b:08x}, "
        f"op=0b{operation:03b}, expected=0x{expected:08x}, "
        f"actual=0x{actual:08x}"
    )
    return actual

# `alu32` Microarchitecture Specification

## 1. Block Overview

- **Block name:** `alu32`
- **Function:** `alu32` is a stateless 32-bit combinational arithmetic/logic unit. It accepts two 32-bit operands and a 3-bit operation selector, and produces one 32-bit result. The supported operations are modulo-`2^32` addition, modulo-`2^32` subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, and bitwise XOR. No carry, borrow, signed-overflow, zero, or comparison flags are generated because none were requested.
- **Latency:** 0 clock cycles. The output changes combinationally after an input change and settles after the combinational propagation delay.
- **Throughput:** One independent operation per integration clock cycle (`1.0 operation/cycle`) when placed between synchronous source and destination registers. There is no internal initiation restriction.
- **Pipeline depth:** 0 registered stages; one logical combinational evaluation stage.
- **Interface protocol:** Simple dedicated pins. The supplied requirements describe a standalone ALU and do not require a bus, streaming protocol, valid/ready flow control, or packet framing. No separate ERS, frozen interface-contract file, FRD, block diagram, or neighboring-block description exists in the workspace; consequently, Section 2 establishes the minimal standalone port contract needed by the requested function.
- **Golden model:** No Python golden model exists. The Boolean and modulo-arithmetic equations in Section 4 are the functional reference for RTL and DV.
- **Clock/reset:** The block contains no state, registers, latches, memories, or FSM. Therefore `clk` and `rst_n` are intentionally absent. The requirement for synchronous active-low `rst_n` applies only when state is present.

## 2. Interface Specification

All ports are unhandshaked dedicated pins. Inputs form one atomic combinational tuple: `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `operation` must refer to the same requested operation. `result` is meaningful whenever those three inputs are stable; there is no separate validity signal.

| Port | Direction | Width | Protocol | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `operand_a` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | First operand, `operand_a[31:0]`. Treated as an unscaled 32-bit bit vector. For ADD/SUB it participates in modulo-`2^32` arithmetic; the same bits may also be interpreted as two's-complement by a consumer because the low 32 result bits are identical. |
| `operand_b` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | Second operand, `operand_b[31:0]`, with the same numeric interpretation as `operand_a`. |
| `operation` | Input | 3 | Dedicated pins | Operation code: `3'b000` ADD, `3'b001` SUB, `3'b010` AND, `3'b011` OR, `3'b100` XOR, and `3'b101` through `3'b111` RESERVED. |
| `result` | Output | 32 | Dedicated pins | Combinational result. ADD and SUB return the low 32 bits (wrap modulo `2^32`); AND/OR/XOR operate independently on each bit. Reserved operation codes return `32'h0000_0000`. |

There are no implicit ports, flags, clock, reset, valid/ready, or error sidebands. If a later integration contract requires differently named ports or flags, the contract and this specification must be revised together; aliases must not be added silently.

## 3. Microarchitecture

### 3.1 Top-Level Block Diagram

```text
                         operation[2:0]
                              |
                              v
                       +--------------+
                       | exact opcode |
                       | decoder      |
                       +------+-------+
                              |
             sub_sel ---------+------------------------------+
                |                                            |
                v                                            v
operand_b --> [32 XOR gates] --> b_mod[31:0]         +----------------+
                ^                                    | AND / OR / XOR |
                |                                    | 32-bit logic   |
                +-- {32{sub_sel}}                    +-------+--------+
                                                            |
operand_a --> zero extend --+                                |
                            v                                |
                       +-----------+                         |
b_mod --> zero extend ->| 33-bit   |--> arith_ext[32:0]      |
sub_sel --> carry-in -->| adder     |--> arith_low[31:0]      |
                       +-----+-----+                         |
                             |                               |
                             +---------------+---------------+
                                             v
                                      +-------------+
operation[2:0] ---------------------->| 32-bit      |--> result[31:0]
                                      | result mux  |
                                      +-------------+
```

The add and subtract operations share one 33-bit adder. The bitwise functions may be synthesized as parallel gates feeding the result mux. The opcode decode uses exact equality comparisons; no wildcard (`casex`/`casez`) decode is permitted.

### 3.2 Datapath

#### Number formats

- `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `result` are plain 32-bit unscaled bit vectors; fixed-point Q notation is not applicable.
- Arithmetic is modulo `2^32`. This definition is valid for both unsigned and two's-complement operand interpretations when only the low 32 result bits are retained.
- Intermediate widening uses zero extension because the implementation is explicitly performing unsigned modulo arithmetic. There is no implicit signed cast.

#### Shared add/sub datapath

Define these exact combinational nodes:

```text
sub_sel       = (operation == 3'b001)                 // 1 bit
a_ext         = {1'b0, operand_a}                     // 33 bits unsigned
b_mod         = operand_b XOR {32{sub_sel}}           // 32 bits
b_mod_ext     = {1'b0, b_mod}                         // 33 bits unsigned
carry_in_ext  = {32'b0, sub_sel}                      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_ext     = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_low     = arith_ext[31:0]                       // 32 bits
```

- For ADD, `sub_sel=0`, so `arith_ext = {0,A}+{0,B}`.
- For SUB, `sub_sel=1`, so the low 32 bits implement `A + ~B + 1 = A-B (mod 2^32)`.
- `arith_ext[32]` is deliberately discarded. For ADD it is the carry-out. For SUB no borrow/carry flag is exposed.
- No saturation or rounding occurs. Width reduction from 33 to 32 bits is explicit truncation of the most-significant carry bit, producing wraparound modulo `2^32`.

#### Bit-width derivation

| Node/operation | Input range | Mathematical range | Hardware width and policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a_ext`, `b_mod_ext` | `0` to `2^32-1` | Same | 33-bit unsigned, zero-extended |
| ADD exact sum | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `0..2^33-2` | 33-bit unsigned `arith_ext`; output truncates to 32 bits (wrap) |
| SUB mathematical difference | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `-(2^32-1)..+(2^32-1)` | Implemented by a 33-bit unsigned two's-complement adder; low 32 bits are exact modulo-`2^32` difference |
| AND/OR/XOR | Two 32-bit vectors | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits, no growth, no overflow |
| Opcode result mux | Five 32-bit candidates plus zero | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits; no truncation |

#### Bitwise datapath and result selection

```text
and_result = operand_a & operand_b     // 32 bits
or_result  = operand_a | operand_b     // 32 bits
xor_result = operand_a ^ operand_b     // 32 bits
```

The final combinational selection is:

| `operation` | Mnemonic | `result` equation |
|---:|---|---|
| `3'b000` | ADD | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=0` |
| `3'b001` | SUB | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=1` |
| `3'b010` | AND | `operand_a & operand_b` |
| `3'b011` | OR | `operand_a | operand_b` |
| `3'b100` | XOR | `operand_a ^ operand_b` |
| `3'b101` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b110` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b111` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |

RTL must assign a default of `32'h0000_0000` before or in the `default` arm of a complete combinational `case` so no latch is inferred.

### 3.3 Control Logic

No FSM is required. There is no sequential control, command pulse, busy/done status, handshake, buffering, or backpressure.

The only control is combinational opcode decode:

- `sub_sel` is asserted only for `operation == 3'b001`.
- A complete `case (operation)` selects exactly one result equation.
- Reserved binary opcode values select zero.
- `operation` is consumed in the same combinational interval in which it is decoded, so there is no later FSM state and no decoded decision that needs to be latched.
- Implement using `always @*` with blocking assignments, or equivalent continuous assignments compatible with Verilog-2005. Do not use SystemVerilog `always_comb`, `logic`, `unique case`, or enumerated types.

### 3.4 Storage Elements

There are no registers, arrays, FIFOs, register files, ROMs, LUT memories, SRAMs, or other storage elements. Boolean gates used for bitwise operations are logic, not a lookup-table memory. Accordingly, the memory manifest is empty.

- **Registers:** none.
- **Memories:** none.
- **FSM state:** none.
- **`flip_flop_budget`:** exactly `0 FF`. The implemented RTL must remain combinational and synthesis must report zero inferred latches and zero inferred flip-flops for this module.
- **`sram_budget`:** `0 bits (0 KiB)`, zero macros.
- **ROM budget:** `0 bits`.

No storage geometry reaches the 2-Kbit SRAM threshold, and no CoreSmith memory primitive is needed.

## 4. Algorithm Mapping

No Python golden model was supplied and none exists. The following mapping is from the requested functional description to hardware; it is the complete reference behavior.

| Functional requirement | Hardware mapping |
|---|---|
| 32-bit addition | One shared 33-bit adder, `A+B`, followed by explicit selection of bits `[31:0]` |
| 32-bit subtraction | The same 33-bit adder using `A+(~B)+1`; select bits `[31:0]` |
| Bitwise AND | 32 parallel two-input AND functions |
| Bitwise OR | 32 parallel two-input OR functions |
| Bitwise XOR | 32 parallel two-input XOR functions |
| Choose operation | Complete 3-bit combinational opcode decoder and 32-bit result mux |
| Unsupported opcode | Constant-zero mux input |

There are no loops, dynamic lists, exceptions, dictionaries, floating-point values, divisions, shifts, casts, coefficient tables, or iteration-order semantics to map.

Reference equations for bit-exact verification, with all operations masked to 32 bits:

```text
ADD: result = (operand_a + operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
SUB: result = (operand_a - operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
AND: result =  operand_a & operand_b
OR:  result =  operand_a | operand_b
XOR: result =  operand_a ^ operand_b
RESERVED: result = 32'h0000_0000
```

### 4a. Cross-Block Semantic Invariants (MANDATORY)

No architecture connection graph or neighboring block is supplied. Therefore there is no named cross-block feedback, context, packet ordering, frame geometry, or adaptive state to preserve. It is safe for this block to be stateless because every output is a pure function of the current input tuple and no prior operation affects a later one. - There are no registers or memories to initialize.
- There is no reset port. The specified synchronous active-low reset convention is inapplicable because the block is entirely combinational.
- There is no multi-cycle initialization sequence.

_MASK32 = (1 << 32) - 1

def _spec_reference(operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int) -> int:
    """Fallback oracle: the exact equations designated by uArch section 4."""
    operand_a &= _MASK32
    operand_b &= _MASK32
    operation &= 0x7
    if operation == 0:
        return (operand_a + operand_b) & _MASK32
    if operation == 1:
        return (operand_a - operand_b) & _MASK32
    if operation == 2:
        return operand_a & operand_b
    if operation == 3:
        return operand_a | operand_b
    if operation == 4:
        return operand_a ^ operand_b
    return 0

    if _golden_alu32 is not None:

    return _spec_reference(operand_a, operand_b, operation)

/*
 * Block: alu32
 * Description: Stateless 32-bit combinational arithmetic/logic unit.
 *              ADD and SUB wrap modulo 2^32. Reserved operation codes
 *              produce zero.
 *
 * I/O ports:
 *   operand_a [31:0] - First arithmetic/logic operand.
 *   operand_b [31:0] - Second arithmetic/logic operand.
 *   operation  [2:0] - 000 ADD, 001 SUB, 010 AND, 011 OR, 100 XOR.
 *   result    [31:0] - Selected combinational result.
 *
 * Every data-transforming output is derived from operand_a and operand_b.
 * The authoritative interface is combinational and declares no clock,
 * reset, handshake, metadata, packet-boundary, or error ports.
 */
module alu32 (
    input  wire [31:0] operand_a,
    input  wire [31:0] operand_b,
    input  wire [2:0]  operation,
    output reg  [31:0] result
);

    /* Named exact-decode predicates are retained for VCD auditability. */
    wire add_sel;
    wire sub_sel;
    wire and_sel;
    wire or_sel;
    wire xor_sel;
    wire reserved_opcode;

    /*
     * Shared unsigned add/sub datapath. All operands are explicitly widened
     * to 33 bits; arith_low explicitly implements modulo-2^32 truncation.
     */
    wire [32:0] a_ext;
    wire [31:0] b_mod;
    wire [32:0] b_mod_ext;
    wire [32:0] carry_in_ext;
    wire [32:0] arith_ext;
    wire [31:0] arith_low;
    wire        arith_carry_discarded;

    wire [31:0] and_result;
    wire [31:0] or_result;
    wire [31:0] xor_result;

    assign add_sel         = (operation == 3'b000);
    assign sub_sel         = (operation == 3'b001);
    assign and_sel         = (operation == 3'b010);
    assign or_sel          = (operation == 3'b011);
    assign xor_sel         = (operation == 3'b100);
    assign reserved_opcode = !(add_sel || sub_sel || and_sel ||
                               or_sel || xor_sel);

    assign a_ext        = {1'b0, operand_a};
    assign b_mod        = operand_b ^ {32{sub_sel}};
    assign b_mod_ext    = {1'b0, b_mod};
    assign carry_in_ext = {32'b00000000000000000000000000000000,

    assign arith_low    = arith_ext[31:0];

    assign or_result  = operand_a | operand_b;

# `alu32` Microarchitecture Specification

## 1. Block Overview

- **Block name:** `alu32`
- **Function:** `alu32` is a stateless 32-bit combinational arithmetic/logic unit. It accepts two 32-bit operands and a 3-bit operation selector, and produces one 32-bit result. The supported operations are modulo-`2^32` addition, modulo-`2^32` subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, and bitwise XOR. No carry, borrow, signed-overflow, zero, or comparison flags are generated because none were requested.
- **Latency:** 0 clock cycles. The output changes combinationally after an input change and settles after the combinational propagation delay.
- **Throughput:** One independent operation per integration clock cycle (`1.0 operation/cycle`) when placed between synchronous source and destination registers. There is no internal initiation restriction.
- **Pipeline depth:** 0 registered stages; one logical combinational evaluation stage.
- **Interface protocol:** Simple dedicated pins. The supplied requirements describe a standalone ALU and do not require a bus, streaming protocol, valid/ready flow control, or packet framing. No separate ERS, frozen interface-contract file, FRD, block diagram, or neighboring-block description exists in the workspace; consequently, Section 2 establishes the minimal standalone port contract needed by the requested function.
- **Golden model:** No Python golden model exists. The Boolean and modulo-arithmetic equations in Section 4 are the functional reference for RTL and DV.
- **Clock/reset:** The block contains no state, registers, latches, memories, or FSM. Therefore `clk` and `rst_n` are intentionally absent. The requirement for synchronous active-low `rst_n` applies only when state is present.

## 2. Interface Specification

All ports are unhandshaked dedicated pins. Inputs form one atomic combinational tuple: `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `operation` must refer to the same requested operation. `result` is meaningful whenever those three inputs are stable; there is no separate validity signal.

| Port | Direction | Width | Protocol | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `operand_a` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | First operand, `operand_a[31:0]`. Treated as an unscaled 32-bit bit vector. For ADD/SUB it participates in modulo-`2^32` arithmetic; the same bits may also be interpreted as two's-complement by a consumer because the low 32 result bits are identical. |
| `operand_b` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | Second operand, `operand_b[31:0]`, with the same numeric interpretation as `operand_a`. |
| `operation` | Input | 3 | Dedicated pins | Operation code: `3'b000` ADD, `3'b001` SUB, `3'b010` AND, `3'b011` OR, `3'b100` XOR, and `3'b101` through `3'b111` RESERVED. |
| `result` | Output | 32 | Dedicated pins | Combinational result. ADD and SUB return the low 32 bits (wrap modulo `2^32`); AND/OR/XOR operate independently on each bit. Reserved operation codes return `32'h0000_0000`. |

There are no implicit ports, flags, clock, reset, valid/ready, or error sidebands. If a later integration contract requires differently named ports or flags, the contract and this specification must be revised together; aliases must not be added silently.

## 3. Microarchitecture

### 3.1 Top-Level Block Diagram

```text
                         operation[2:0]
                              |
                              v
                       +--------------+
                       | exact opcode |
                       | decoder      |
                       +------+-------+
                              |
             sub_sel ---------+------------------------------+
                |                                            |
                v                                            v
operand_b --> [32 XOR gates] --> b_mod[31:0]         +----------------+
                ^                                    | AND / OR / XOR |
                |                                    | 32-bit logic   |
                +-- {32{sub_sel}}                    +-------+--------+
                                                            |
operand_a --> zero extend --+                                |
                            v                                |
                       +-----------+                         |
b_mod --> zero extend ->| 33-bit   |--> arith_ext[32:0]      |
sub_sel --> carry-in -->| adder     |--> arith_low[31:0]      |
                       +-----+-----+                         |
                             |                               |
                             +---------------+---------------+
                                             v
                                      +-------------+
operation[2:0] ---------------------->| 32-bit      |--> result[31:0]
                                      | result mux  |
                                      +-------------+
```

The add and subtract operations share one 33-bit adder. The bitwise functions may be synthesized as parallel gates feeding the result mux. The opcode decode uses exact equality comparisons; no wildcard (`casex`/`casez`) decode is permitted.

### 3.2 Datapath

#### Number formats

- `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `result` are plain 32-bit unscaled bit vectors; fixed-point Q notation is not applicable.
- Arithmetic is modulo `2^32`. This definition is valid for both unsigned and two's-complement operand interpretations when only the low 32 result bits are retained.
- Intermediate widening uses zero extension because the implementation is explicitly performing unsigned modulo arithmetic. There is no implicit signed cast.

#### Shared add/sub datapath

Define these exact combinational nodes:

```text
sub_sel       = (operation == 3'b001)                 // 1 bit
a_ext         = {1'b0, operand_a}                     // 33 bits unsigned
b_mod         = operand_b XOR {32{sub_sel}}           // 32 bits
b_mod_ext     = {1'b0, b_mod}                         // 33 bits unsigned
carry_in_ext  = {32'b0, sub_sel}                      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_ext     = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_low     = arith_ext[31:0]                       // 32 bits
```

- For ADD, `sub_sel=0`, so `arith_ext = {0,A}+{0,B}`.
- For SUB, `sub_sel=1`, so the low 32 bits implement `A + ~B + 1 = A-B (mod 2^32)`.
- `arith_ext[32]` is deliberately discarded. For ADD it is the carry-out. For SUB no borrow/carry flag is exposed.
- No saturation or rounding occurs. Width reduction from 33 to 32 bits is explicit truncation of the most-significant carry bit, producing wraparound modulo `2^32`.

#### Bit-width derivation

| Node/operation | Input range | Mathematical range | Hardware width and policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a_ext`, `b_mod_ext` | `0` to `2^32-1` | Same | 33-bit unsigned, zero-extended |
| ADD exact sum | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `0..2^33-2` | 33-bit unsigned `arith_ext`; output truncates to 32 bits (wrap) |
| SUB mathematical difference | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `-(2^32-1)..+(2^32-1)` | Implemented by a 33-bit unsigned two's-complement adder; low 32 bits are exact modulo-`2^32` difference |
| AND/OR/XOR | Two 32-bit vectors | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits, no growth, no overflow |
| Opcode result mux | Five 32-bit candidates plus zero | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits; no truncation |

#### Bitwise datapath and result selection

```text
and_result = operand_a & operand_b     // 32 bits
or_result  = operand_a | operand_b     // 32 bits
xor_result = operand_a ^ operand_b     // 32 bits
```

The final combinational selection is:

| `operation` | Mnemonic | `result` equation |
|---:|---|---|
| `3'b000` | ADD | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=0` |
| `3'b001` | SUB | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=1` |
| `3'b010` | AND | `operand_a & operand_b` |
| `3'b011` | OR | `operand_a | operand_b` |
| `3'b100` | XOR | `operand_a ^ operand_b` |
| `3'b101` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b110` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b111` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |

RTL must assign a default of `32'h0000_0000` before or in the `default` arm of a complete combinational `case` so no latch is inferred.

### 3.3 Control Logic

No FSM is required. There is no sequential control, command pulse, busy/done status, handshake, buffering, or backpressure.

The only control is combinational opcode decode:

- `sub_sel` is asserted only for `operation == 3'b001`.
- A complete `case (operation)` selects exactly one result equation.
- Reserved binary opcode values select zero.
- `operation` is consumed in the same combinational interval in which it is decoded, so there is no later FSM state and no decoded decision that needs to be latched.
- Implement using `always @*` with blocking assignments, or equivalent continuous assignments compatible with Verilog-2005. Do not use SystemVerilog `always_comb`, `logic`, `unique case`, or enumerated types.

### 3.4 Storage Elements

There are no registers, arrays, FIFOs, register files, ROMs, LUT memories, SRAMs, or other storage elements. Boolean gates used for bitwise operations are logic, not a lookup-table memory. Accordingly, the memory manifest is empty.

- **Registers:** none.
- **Memories:** none.
- **FSM state:** none.
- **`flip_flop_budget`:** exactly `0 FF`. The implemented RTL must remain combinational and synthesis must report zero inferred latches and zero inferred flip-flops for this module.
- **`sram_budget`:** `0 bits (0 KiB)`, zero macros.
- **ROM budget:** `0 bits`.

No storage geometry reaches the 2-Kbit SRAM threshold, and no CoreSmith memory primitive is needed.

## 4. Algorithm Mapping

No Python golden model was supplied and none exists. The following mapping is from the requested functional description to hardware; it is the complete reference behavior.

| Functional requirement | Hardware mapping |
|---|---|
| 32-bit addition | One shared 33-bit adder, `A+B`, followed by explicit selection of bits `[31:0]` |
| 32-bit subtraction | The same 33-bit adder using `A+(~B)+1`; select bits `[31:0]` |
| Bitwise AND | 32 parallel two-input AND functions |
| Bitwise OR | 32 parallel two-input OR functions |
| Bitwise XOR | 32 parallel two-input XOR functions |
| Choose operation | Complete 3-bit combinational opcode decoder and 32-bit result mux |
| Unsupported opcode | Constant-zero mux input |

There are no loops, dynamic lists, exceptions, dictionaries, floating-point values, divisions, shifts, casts, coefficient tables, or iteration-order semantics to map.

Reference equations for bit-exact verification, with all operations masked to 32 bits:

```text
ADD: result = (operand_a + operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
SUB: result = (operand_a - operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
AND: result =  operand_a & operand_b
OR:  result =  operand_a | operand_b
XOR: result =  operand_a ^ operand_b
RESERVED: result = 32'h0000_0000
```

### 4a. Cross-Block Semantic Invariants (MANDATORY)

No architecture connection graph or neighboring block is supplied. Therefore there is no named cross-block feedback, context, packet ordering, frame geometry, or adaptive state to preserve. It is safe for this block to be stateless because every output is a pure function of the current input tuple and no prior operation affects a later one. The interface-level invariants below are nevertheless mandatory for any eventual producer and consumer.

- **Applies to ports/state:** `operand_a`, `operand_b`, `operation`, and `result`; no internal state.
- **Invariant:** `result` must be computed from the same concurrently presented values of all three inputs. Mixing an old operand with a new opcode is outside the interface contract.
- **Golden reference point:** The equations in Section 4; no Python golden model exists.

- **Update/consume timing:** Combinational. A consumer may sample `result` only after all inputs and the combinational path meet its setup requirement at the consumer's capture edge.

## 5. Reset and Initialization

- There are no registers or memories to initialize.
- There is no reset port. The specified synchronous active-low reset convention is inapplicable because the block is entirely combinational.
- There is no multi-cycle initialization sequence.
- During a chip-level reset, `result` continues to be the combinational function of the ALU inputs. The integrating source must drive known inputs if a known reset-time result is required.

- **Target technology:** SkyWater Sky130, `sky130_fd_sc_hd` standard-cell library.

def _spec_reference(operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int) -> int:
    """Fallback oracle: the exact equations designated by uArch section 4."""
    operand_a &= _MASK32
    operand_b &= _MASK32

    if operation == 1:

    if operation == 2:

    if operation == 3:
        return operand_a | operand_b
    if operation == 4:
        return operand_a ^ operand_b
    return 0

/*
 * Block: alu32
 * Description: Stateless 32-bit combinational arithmetic/logic unit.
 *              ADD and SUB wrap modulo 2^32. Reserved operation codes
 *              produce zero.
 *
 * I/O ports:
 *   operand_a [31:0] - First arithmetic/logic operand.
 *   operand_b [31:0] - Second arithmetic/logic operand.
 *   operation  [2:0] - 000 ADD, 001 SUB, 010 AND, 011 OR, 100 XOR.
 *   result    [31:0] - Selected combinational result.
 *
 * Every data-transforming output is derived from operand_a and operand_b.
 * The authoritative interface is combinational and declares no clock,
 * reset, handshake, metadata, packet-boundary, or error ports.
 */
module alu32 (
    input  wire [31:0] operand_a,
    input  wire [31:0] operand_b,
    input  wire [2:0]  operation,
    output reg  [31:0] result
);

    /* Named exact-decode predicates are retained for VCD auditability. */
    wire add_sel;
    wire sub_sel;
    wire and_sel;
    wire or_sel;
    wire xor_sel;
    wire reserved_opcode;

    /*
     * Shared unsigned add/sub datapath. All operands are explicitly widened
     * to 33 bits; arith_low explicitly implements modulo-2^32 truncation.
     */
    wire [32:0] a_ext;
    wire [31:0] b_mod;
    wire [32:0] b_mod_ext;
    wire [32:0] carry_in_ext;
    wire [32:0] arith_ext;
    wire [31:0] arith_low;
    wire        arith_carry_discarded;

    wire [31:0] and_result;
    wire [31:0] or_result;
    wire [31:0] xor_result;

    assign add_sel         = (operation == 3'b000);
    assign sub_sel         = (operation == 3'b001);
    assign and_sel         = (operation == 3'b010);
    assign or_sel          = (operation == 3'b011);
    assign xor_sel         = (operation == 3'b100);
    assign reserved_opcode = !(add_sel || sub_sel || and_sel ||
                               or_sel || xor_sel);

    assign a_ext        = {1'b0, operand_a};
    assign b_mod        = operand_b ^ {32{sub_sel}};
    assign b_mod_ext    = {1'b0, b_mod};
    assign carry_in_ext = {32'b00000000000000000000000000000000,
                           sub_sel};
    assign arith_ext    = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext;
    assign arith_low    = arith_ext[31:0];
    assign arith_carry_discarded = arith_ext[32];

    assign and_result = operand_a & operand_b;
    assign or_result  = operand_a | operand_b;
    assign xor_result = operand_a ^ operand_b;

    /* Complete exact decode supplies a value on every path: no latch. */
    always @(*) begin
        result = 32'h0000_0000;
        case (operation)
            3'b000: result = arith_low;
            3'b001: result = arith_low;
            3'b010: result = and_result;
            3'b011: result = or_result;
            3'b100: result = xor_result;
            3'b101: result = 32'h0000_0000;
            3'b110: result = 32'h0000_0000;
            3'b111: result = 32'h0000_0000;
            default: result = 32'h0000_0000;
        endcase
    end

# `alu32` Microarchitecture Specification

## 1. Block Overview

- **Block name:** `alu32`
- **Function:** `alu32` is a stateless 32-bit combinational arithmetic/logic unit. It accepts two 32-bit operands and a 3-bit operation selector, and produces one 32-bit result. The supported operations are modulo-`2^32` addition, modulo-`2^32` subtraction, bitwise AND, bitwise OR, and bitwise XOR. No carry, borrow, signed-overflow, zero, or comparison flags are generated because none were requested.
- **Latency:** 0 clock cycles. The output changes combinationally after an input change and settles after the combinational propagation delay.
- **Throughput:** One independent operation per integration clock cycle (`1.0 operation/cycle`) when placed between synchronous source and destination registers. There is no internal initiation restriction.
- **Pipeline depth:** 0 registered stages; one logical combinational evaluation stage.
- **Interface protocol:** Simple dedicated pins. The supplied requirements describe a standalone ALU and do not require a bus, streaming protocol, valid/ready flow control, or packet framing. No separate ERS, frozen interface-contract file, FRD, block diagram, or neighboring-block description exists in the workspace; consequently, Section 2 establishes the minimal standalone port contract needed by the requested function.
- **Golden model:** No Python golden model exists. The Boolean and modulo-arithmetic equations in Section 4 are the functional reference for RTL and DV.
- **Clock/reset:** The block contains no state, registers, latches, memories, or FSM. Therefore `clk` and `rst_n` are intentionally absent. The requirement for synchronous active-low `rst_n` applies only when state is present.

## 2. Interface Specification

All ports are unhandshaked dedicated pins. Inputs form one atomic combinational tuple: `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `operation` must refer to the same requested operation. `result` is meaningful whenever those three inputs are stable; there is no separate validity signal.

| Port | Direction | Width | Protocol | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `operand_a` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | First operand, `operand_a[31:0]`. Treated as an unscaled 32-bit bit vector. For ADD/SUB it participates in modulo-`2^32` arithmetic; the same bits may also be interpreted as two's-complement by a consumer because the low 32 result bits are identical. |
| `operand_b` | Input | 32 | Dedicated pins | Second operand, `operand_b[31:0]`, with the same numeric interpretation as `operand_a`. |
| `operation` | Input | 3 | Dedicated pins | Operation code: `3'b000` ADD, `3'b001` SUB, `3'b010` AND, `3'b011` OR, `3'b100` XOR, and `3'b101` through `3'b111` RESERVED. |
| `result` | Output | 32 | Dedicated pins | Combinational result. ADD and SUB return the low 32 bits (wrap modulo `2^32`); AND/OR/XOR operate independently on each bit. Reserved operation codes return `32'h0000_0000`. |

There are no implicit ports, flags, clock, reset, valid/ready, or error sidebands. If a later integration contract requires differently named ports or flags, the contract and this specification must be revised together; aliases must not be added silently.

## 3. Microarchitecture

### 3.1 Top-Level Block Diagram

```text
                         operation[2:0]
                              |
                              v
                       +--------------+
                       | exact opcode |
                       | decoder      |
                       +------+-------+
                              |
             sub_sel ---------+------------------------------+
                |                                            |
                v                                            v
operand_b --> [32 XOR gates] --> b_mod[31:0]         +----------------+
                ^                                    | AND / OR / XOR |
                |                                    | 32-bit logic   |
                +-- {32{sub_sel}}                    +-------+--------+
                                                            |
operand_a --> zero extend --+                                |
                            v                                |
                       +-----------+                         |
b_mod --> zero extend ->| 33-bit   |--> arith_ext[32:0]      |
sub_sel --> carry-in -->| adder     |--> arith_low[31:0]      |
                       +-----+-----+                         |
                             |                               |
                             +---------------+---------------+
                                             v
                                      +-------------+
operation[2:0] ---------------------->| 32-bit      |--> result[31:0]
                                      | result mux  |
                                      +-------------+
```

The add and subtract operations share one 33-bit adder. The bitwise functions may be synthesized as parallel gates feeding the result mux. The opcode decode uses exact equality comparisons; no wildcard (`casex`/`casez`) decode is permitted.

### 3.2 Datapath

#### Number formats

- `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `result` are plain 32-bit unscaled bit vectors; fixed-point Q notation is not applicable.
- Arithmetic is modulo `2^32`. This definition is valid for both unsigned and two's-complement operand interpretations when only the low 32 result bits are retained.
- Intermediate widening uses zero extension because the implementation is explicitly performing unsigned modulo arithmetic. There is no implicit signed cast.

#### Shared add/sub datapath

Define these exact combinational nodes:

```text
sub_sel       = (operation == 3'b001)                 // 1 bit
a_ext         = {1'b0, operand_a}                     // 33 bits unsigned
b_mod         = operand_b XOR {32{sub_sel}}           // 32 bits
b_mod_ext     = {1'b0, b_mod}                         // 33 bits unsigned
carry_in_ext  = {32'b0, sub_sel}                      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_ext     = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_low     = arith_ext[31:0]                       // 32 bits
```

- For ADD, `sub_sel=0`, so `arith_ext = {0,A}+{0,B}`.
- For SUB, `sub_sel=1`, so the low 32 bits implement `A + ~B + 1 = A-B (mod 2^32)`.
- `arith_ext[32]` is deliberately discarded. For ADD it is the carry-out. For SUB no borrow/carry flag is exposed.
- No saturation or rounding occurs. Width reduction from 33 to 32 bits is explicit truncation of the most-significant carry bit, producing wraparound modulo `2^32`.

#### Bit-width derivation

| Node/operation | Input range | Mathematical range | Hardware width and policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a_ext`, `b_mod_ext` | `0` to `2^32-1` | Same | 33-bit unsigned, zero-extended |
| ADD exact sum | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `0..2^33-2` | 33-bit unsigned `arith_ext`; output truncates to 32 bits (wrap) |
| SUB mathematical difference | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `-(2^32-1)..+(2^32-1)` | Implemented by a 33-bit unsigned two's-complement adder; low 32 bits are exact modulo-`2^32` difference |
| AND/OR/XOR | Two 32-bit vectors | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits, no growth, no overflow |
| Opcode result mux | Five 32-bit candidates plus zero | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits; no truncation |

#### Bitwise datapath and result selection

```text
and_result = operand_a & operand_b     // 32 bits
or_result  = operand_a | operand_b     // 32 bits
xor_result = operand_a ^ operand_b     // 32 bits
```

The final combinational selection is:

| `operation` | Mnemonic | `result` equation |
|---:|---|---|
| `3'b000` | ADD | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=0` |
| `3'b001` | SUB | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=1` |
| `3'b010` | AND | `operand_a & operand_b` |
| `3'b011` | OR | `operand_a | operand_b` |
| `3'b100` | XOR | `operand_a ^ operand_b` |
| `3'b101` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b110` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |
| `3'b111` | RESERVED | `32'h0000_0000` |

RTL must assign a default of `32'h0000_0000` before or in the `default` arm of a complete combinational `case` so no latch is inferred.

### 3.3 Control Logic

No FSM is required. There is no sequential control, command pulse, busy/done status, handshake, buffering, or backpressure.

The only control is combinational opcode decode:

- `sub_sel` is asserted only for `operation == 3'b001`.
- A complete `case (operation)` selects exactly one result equation.
- Reserved binary opcode values select zero.
- `operation` is consumed in the same combinational interval in which it is decoded, so there is no later FSM state and no decoded decision that needs to be latched.
- Implement using `always @*` with blocking assignments, or equivalent continuous assignments compatible with Verilog-2005. Do not use SystemVerilog `always_comb`, `logic`, `unique case`, or enumerated types.

### 3.4 Storage Elements

There are no registers, arrays, FIFOs, register files, ROMs, LUT memories, SRAMs, or other storage elements. Boolean gates used for bitwise operations are logic, not a lookup-table memory. Accordingly, the memory manifest is empty.

- **Registers:** none.
- **Memories:** none.
- **FSM state:** none.
- **`flip_flop_budget`:** exactly `0 FF`. The implemented RTL must remain combinational and synthesis must report zero inferred latches and zero inferred flip-flops for this module.
- **`sram_budget`:** `0 bits (0 KiB)`, zero macros.
- **ROM budget:** `0 bits`.

No storage geometry reaches the 2-Kbit SRAM threshold, and no CoreSmith memory primitive is needed.

## 4. Algorithm Mapping

No Python golden model was supplied and none exists. The following mapping is from the requested functional description to hardware; it is the complete reference behavior.

| Functional requirement | Hardware mapping |
|---|---|
| 32-bit addition | One shared 33-bit adder, `A+B`, followed by explicit selection of bits `[31:0]` |
| 32-bit subtraction | The same 33-bit adder using `A+(~B)+1`; select bits `[31:0]` |
| Bitwise AND | 32 parallel two-input AND functions |
| Bitwise OR | 32 parallel two-input OR functions |
| Bitwise XOR | 32 parallel two-input XOR functions |
| Choose operation | Complete 3-bit combinational opcode decoder and 32-bit result mux |
| Unsupported opcode | Constant-zero mux input |

There are no loops, dynamic lists, exceptions, dictionaries, floating-point values, divisions, shifts, casts, coefficient tables, or iteration-order semantics to map.

Reference equations for bit-exact verification, with all operations masked to 32 bits:

```text
ADD: result = (operand_a + operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
SUB: result = (operand_a - operand_b) & 32'hFFFF_FFFF
AND: result =  operand_a & operand_b
OR:  result =  operand_a | operand_b
XOR: result =  operand_a ^ operand_b
RESERVED: result = 32'h0000_0000
```

### 4a. Cross-Block Semantic Invariants (MANDATORY)

No architecture connection graph or neighboring block is supplied. Therefore there is no named cross-block feedback, context, packet ordering, frame geometry, or adaptive state to preserve. It is safe for this block to be stateless because every output is a pure function of the current input tuple and no prior operation affects a later one. The interface-level invariants below are nevertheless mandatory for any eventual producer and consumer.

#### `INV-ALU-ATOMIC-001` — input tuple atomicity

- **Applies to ports/state:** `operand_a`, `operand_b`, `operation`, and `result`; no internal state.
- **Invariant:** `result` must be computed from the same concurrently presented values of all three inputs. Mixing an old operand with a new opcode is outside the interface contract.
- **Golden reference point:** The equations in Section 4; no Python golden model exists.
- **Tolerance:** Exact 32-bit equality.
- **Update/consume timing:** Combinational. A consumer may sample `result` only after all inputs and the combinational path meet its setup requirement at the consumer's capture edge.
- **Downstream dependency:** No downstream block was named. Any future consumer depends on this tuple alignment.
- **Validation hook:** Dump and compare the four top-level ports in the same simulation timestep; assert `result === alu_reference(operand_a, operand_b, operation)` after a combinational settle delay.

#### `INV-ALU-OPMAP-002` — opcode mapping

- **Applies to ports/state:** `operation[2:0]` and `result[31:0]`.
- **Invariant:** The eight-entry mapping in Section 3.2 is fixed. In particular, `001` means SUB and `100` means XOR; reserved encodings return zero.

- **Applies to ports/state:** `operand_a`, `operand_b`, internal `arith_ext[32:0]`, and `result`.
- **Invariant:** ADD/SUB wrap modulo `2^32`. They do not saturate, trap, or expose carry/borrow.

- **Update/consume timing:** Combinational; `arith_ext[32]` is discarded before result selection.

- **Validation hook:** Expose `arith_ext` in simulation/VCD if practical and test `FFFF_FFFF+1`, `0-1`, `8000_0000-1`, and `7FFF_FFFF+1`.

## 5. Reset and Initialization

- There are no registers or memories to initialize.
- There is no reset port. The specified synchronous active-low reset convention is inapplicable because the block is entirely combinational.
- There is no multi-cycle initialization sequence.
- During a chip-level reset, `result` continues to be the combinational function of the ALU inputs. The integrating source must drive known inputs if a known reset-time result is required.
- There are no valid, done, drained, packet-complete, frame-complete, or terminal flags. Thus reset-idle cannot be confused with completion.
- The first meaningful result is available with latency 0 as soon as the inputs are stable, including immediately after an external reset is deasserted.

- **Target technology:** SkyWater Sky130, `sky130_fd_sc_hd` standard-cell library.
- **Target frequency:** 50 MHz, corresponding to a 20 ns clock period in the surrounding synchronous system.
- **Critical path:** `operation` decode / conditional `operand_b` inversion → 33-bit carry-propagate add → 32-bit result mux. - **Throughput:** Inputs may change once per integration cycle and the consumer may capture one result every cycle. There is no backpressure and no bubble requirement.

import json
import os
import random

import cocotb
from cocotb.triggers import Timer

# WARNING: model wrapper unavailable; TB-local reference may drift from the block model
# The alu32 uArch explicitly states that no Python golden model exists and
# defines its equations as the authoritative functional reference.
try:
    from alu32_model import alu32 as _golden_alu32
except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
    if exc.name != "alu32_model":
        raise
    _golden_alu32 = None


_DV_SEED = int(os.environ.get("CORESMITH_DV_SEED", "0"), 0)
_MASK32 = (1 << 32) - 1
_SETTLE_NS = 1


def _spec_reference(operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int) -> int:
    """Fallback oracle: the exact equations designated by uArch section 4."""
    operand_a &= _MASK32
    operand_b &= _MASK32
    operation &= 0x7
    if operation == 0:
        return (operand_a + operand_b) & _MASK32
    if operation == 1:
        return (operand_a - operand_b) & _MASK32
    if operation == 2:
        return operand_a & operand_b
    if operation == 3:
        return operand_a | operand_b
    if operation == 4:
        return operand_a ^ operand_b
    return 0


def _model_result(operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int) -> int:
    """Call the supplied model when present, otherwise use its specified fallback."""
    if _golden_alu32 is not None:
        return int(_golden_alu32(int(operand_a), int(operand_b), int(operation))) & _MASK32
    return _spec_reference(operand_a, operand_b, operation)


async def _drive_and_check(dut, operand_a: int, operand_b: int, operation: int,
                           *, context: str) -> int:
    operand_a = int(operand_a) & _MASK32
    operand_b = int(operand_b) & _MASK32
    operation = int(operation) & 0x7
    expected = _model_result(operand_a, operand_b, operation)

    dut.operand_a.value = operand_a
    dut.operand_b.value = operand_b
    dut.operation.value = operation
    await Timer(_SETTLE_NS, unit="ns")

    actual = int(dut.result.value)
    assert actual == expected, (
        f"{context}: A=0x{operand_a:08x}, B=0x{operand_b:08x}, "
        f"op=0b{operation:03b}, expected=0x{expected:08x}, "
        f"actual=0x{actual:08x}"
    )
    return actual

## 7. Edge Cases and Corner Conditions

- `32'hFFFF_FFFF + 32'h0000_0001` returns `32'h0000_0000`; carry is discarded.
- `32'h0000_0000 - 32'h0000_0001` returns `32'hFFFF_FFFF`; borrow is not reported.
- `32'h7FFF_FFFF + 32'h0000_0001` returns `32'h8000_0000`; there is no signed-overflow flag or saturation.
- `32'h8000_0000 - 32'h0000_0001` returns `32'h7FFF_FFFF` modulo `2^32`.
- Bitwise operations apply to all 32 bits without treating bit 31 specially.
- Reserved opcodes `101`, `110`, and `111` return zero. They do not retain a prior result, ensuring no latch or hidden state.
- There is no “empty” or “idle” protocol state; the block is continuously active.
- First sample after external reset deassertion behaves exactly like any other sample and has zero-cycle latency.
- Simulation X/Z values are not architectural input values. For a legal 0/1 opcode and X/Z operand bits, normal four-state operator propagation applies. If `operation` contains X/Z, an exact Verilog `case` falls to the zero default; DV must not treat that simulation-only behavior as a silicon error-detection feature.
- Inputs may glitch and `result` may glitch correspondingly. No asynchronous consumer may rely on glitch-free behavior.

- Use Verilog-2005 constructs only. A recommended style is one `always @*` block with a blocking default assignment and a complete `case`, plus explicitly sized 33-bit intermediate wires for the adder.
- Do not use `casex` or `casez`; those constructs can mask unknown-control bugs in simulation.
- Do not infer latches, add output registers, instantiate tri-state buffers, or use asynchronous reset logic.

- Preserve explicit operand sizing. Both add operands and carry-in must be 33 bits before the addition so Verilog expression-width rules cannot accidentally turn the internal arithmetic into 32 bits.

a_ext         = {1'b0, operand_a}                     // 33 bits unsigned
b_mod         = operand_b XOR {32{sub_sel}}           // 32 bits
b_mod_ext     = {1'b0, b_mod}                         // 33 bits unsigned
carry_in_ext  = {32'b0, sub_sel}                      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_ext     = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_low     = arith_ext[31:0]                       // 32 bits
```

- For ADD, `sub_sel=0`, so `arith_ext = {0,A}+{0,B}`.
- For SUB, `sub_sel=1`, so the low 32 bits implement `A + ~B + 1 = A-B (mod 2^32)`.

- No saturation or rounding occurs. Width reduction from 33 to 32 bits is explicit truncation of the most-significant carry bit, producing wraparound modulo `2^32`.

| SUB mathematical difference | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `-(2^32-1)..+(2^32-1)` | Implemented by a 33-bit unsigned two's-complement adder; low 32 bits are exact modulo-`2^32` difference |

| Opcode result mux | Five 32-bit candidates plus zero | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits; no truncation |

or_result  = operand_a | operand_b     // 32 bits

The add and subtract operations share one 33-bit adder. The bitwise functions may be synthesized as parallel gates feeding the result mux. The opcode decode uses exact equality comparisons; no wildcard (`casex`/`casez`) decode is permitted.

### 3.2 Datapath

#### Number formats

- `operand_a`, `operand_b`, and `result` are plain 32-bit unscaled bit vectors; fixed-point Q notation is not applicable.
- Arithmetic is modulo `2^32`. This definition is valid for both unsigned and two's-complement operand interpretations when only the low 32 result bits are retained.
- Intermediate widening uses zero extension because the implementation is explicitly performing unsigned modulo arithmetic. There is no implicit signed cast.

#### Shared add/sub datapath

Define these exact combinational nodes:

```text
sub_sel       = (operation == 3'b001)                 // 1 bit
a_ext         = {1'b0, operand_a}                     // 33 bits unsigned
b_mod         = operand_b XOR {32{sub_sel}}           // 32 bits
b_mod_ext     = {1'b0, b_mod}                         // 33 bits unsigned
carry_in_ext  = {32'b0, sub_sel}                      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_ext     = a_ext + b_mod_ext + carry_in_ext      // 33 bits unsigned
arith_low     = arith_ext[31:0]                       // 32 bits
```

- For ADD, `sub_sel=0`, so `arith_ext = {0,A}+{0,B}`.
- For SUB, `sub_sel=1`, so the low 32 bits implement `A + ~B + 1 = A-B (mod 2^32)`.
- `arith_ext[32]` is deliberately discarded. For ADD it is the carry-out. For SUB no borrow/carry flag is exposed.
- No saturation or rounding occurs. Width reduction from 33 to 32 bits is explicit truncation of the most-significant carry bit, producing wraparound modulo `2^32`.

| Node/operation | Input range | Mathematical range | Hardware width and policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a_ext`, `b_mod_ext` | `0` to `2^32-1` | Same | 33-bit unsigned, zero-extended |
| ADD exact sum | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `0..2^33-2` | 33-bit unsigned `arith_ext`; output truncates to 32 bits (wrap) |
| SUB mathematical difference | Two values in `0..2^32-1` | `-(2^32-1)..+(2^32-1)` | Implemented by a 33-bit unsigned two's-complement adder; low 32 bits are exact modulo-`2^32` difference |
| AND/OR/XOR | Two 32-bit vectors | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits, no growth, no overflow |
| Opcode result mux | Five 32-bit candidates plus zero | One 32-bit vector | 32 bits; no truncation |

#### Bitwise datapath and result selection

```text
and_result = operand_a & operand_b     // 32 bits
or_result  = operand_a | operand_b     // 32 bits
xor_result = operand_a ^ operand_b     // 32 bits
```

| `operation` | Mnemonic | `result` equation |
|---:|---|---|
| `3'b000` | ADD | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=0` |
| `3'b001` | SUB | `arith_ext[31:0]` with `sub_sel=1` |
| `3'b010` | AND | `operand_a & operand_b` |

 * Each result bit is a function of the current operand sample bits. The
